content:
There is nothing quite like the feeling of standing on your doorstep at 4am, suitcases packed, and realising your taxi has not turned up.

It happens more often than you might think — and it is almost always the result of leaving things to chance. Whether that means booking a last-minute cab through an app, hoping a local driver is available, or relying on a friend who said they would "probably" be free.

If you live in Henfield or the surrounding villages and you have a flight from Gatwick, pre-booking a dedicated airport transfer is the single most effective thing you can do to start your trip on the right foot.

Here is everything you need to know.

How Far Is Henfield from Gatwick Airport?

Henfield sits in the heart of West Sussex, roughly 18 miles south of Gatwick Airport. Under normal conditions, the drive takes around 40 to 50 minutes — typically via the A281 north through Cowfold, then joining the A23 towards the airport.

That said, journey times can vary considerably depending on:

  • Time of day — early morning departures (before 6am) are usually smooth; mid-morning can see heavier traffic on the A23
  • Day of the week — Monday mornings and Friday afternoons tend to be busier
  • Roadworks or incidents — the A23 corridor around Crawley can slow significantly during peak hours
  • Your terminal — Gatwick has both a North and South Terminal, and the transfer between them adds time if you arrive at the wrong one
A good rule of thumb: allow at least 90 minutes from your front door to clearing security, especially for early morning flights.

Why Pre-Booking Your Gatwick Transfer Makes Sense

1. You know exactly what you are paying

With a pre-booked transfer from Western Cars Henfield, your price is agreed upfront. There is no meter running, no surge pricing, and no unpleasant surprise when you arrive at the terminal.

Compare that to ride-hailing apps, where prices can spike significantly during early morning hours or periods of high demand — precisely when most passengers are travelling to the airport.

2. Your driver is there when you need them

When you book in advance, your driver is allocated to your journey specifically. They know your pick-up address, your flight time, and your terminal. There is no waiting for a nearby driver to accept your request.

For early morning departures — the 5am and 6am flights that are so common from Gatwick — this matters enormously. A professional airport transfer service is built around these hours. A general taxi app is not.

3. Flight monitoring means no wasted journeys

Western Cars Henfield monitors your inbound flight when you are returning from a trip. If your flight is delayed, your driver adjusts accordingly. You will not land at Gatwick at midnight to find your taxi left an hour ago.

4. Luggage is never a problem

Airport transfers are designed for travellers. That means saloon cars and larger vehicles with proper boot space, not a hatchback that struggles with two suitcases and a carry-on.

What to Expect When You Book

Booking your Henfield to Gatwick transfer with Western Cars is straightforward:

1. Book online or by phone — use the online booking system at any time, or call 01273 588080 2. Confirm your details — pick-up address, flight number, terminal, and number of passengers 3. Receive your confirmation — you will get a booking reference and driver details ahead of your journey 4. Your driver arrives on time — typically a few minutes early, so you are never rushed

For departures, we recommend being ready at least 5 minutes before your scheduled pick-up time. Your driver will contact you if there are any changes.

Tips for Early Morning Gatwick Flights from Henfield

Early morning flights are popular for good reason — they tend to be cheaper, less crowded, and get you to your destination with the whole day ahead. But they do require a bit of planning.

Allow more time than you think you need. Even at 4am, there can be queues at security, and Gatwick's South Terminal in particular can be busy with long-haul passengers checking in overnight.

Know your terminal before you travel. Gatwick has a North Terminal and a South Terminal, served by different airlines. Check your booking confirmation carefully — easyJet uses the North Terminal, while British Airways and many others use the South. Getting this wrong adds at least 15 minutes to your journey.

Have your booking reference to hand. Your driver will confirm your details, but having your reference number ready speeds things up if there are any last-minute questions.

Pack the night before. It sounds obvious, but a calm, unhurried departure makes a real difference to how the rest of your trip feels.
